documents.title: Universal Guidelines for AI Use in Teaching and Learning: Course Syllabus Template Addendum
tiers: Permitted for Some Activities with Attribution
Permitted for All Activities with Attribution
documents.summary: A provost addendum that urges ethical use, attribution and awareness of licensing terms, then gives instructors three syllabus options for AI: not permitted, permitted for some activities with attribution, or permitted for all activities with attribution. Each option points to the Academic Dishonesty Policy for violations.
documents.stance_why: The addendum sets no single rule: "Faculty members have the flexibility to choose from the following options", which are three tiers (Not Permitted; Permitted for Some Activities with Attribution; Permitted for All Activities with Attribution). Choice is delegated to instructors.

units.why: Opening principle: faculty "should promote ethical use of these tools" when bringing AI into course materials. It is a framework statement addressed to faculty (P56), not a rule on a specific use.
units.anchor: faculty members at the university should promote ethical use of

units.why: "providing proper attribution when AI-generated content is used or presented" is a disclosure duty for AI-generated content; it applies to anyone using or presenting it, so actor is all. P24 fits better than P25 because no tool or prompt details are required here.
units.anchor: providing proper attribution when AI-generated content is used or presented

units.why: "Citations should follow the guidelines specified by academic writing styles such as APA, IEEE, MLA" says how AI attribution is formatted. It names citation styles but not tool, prompt or date, so P24 rather than P25.
units.anchor: Citations should follow the guidelines specified by academic writing styles such as APA, IEEE, MLA

units.why: Faculty "can play a crucial role" in "educating student about the importance of originality" and upholding academic integrity. This asks instructors to explain the reasons for integrity to students (P66), so phase is course-start and modality should.
units.anchor: educating student about
units.policy: Faculty members play a crucial role in educating students about the importance of originality in their work and upholding university values related to academic integrity.

units.why: The text concedes faculty "may not be able to always individually verify the originality of all student work". This is a stated limit on verification, not a ban on detection. It is not P39 or P60, which say detectors are unreliable or staff will not police, so it is UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: may not be able to always individually verify the originality of all student work
units.uncovered_note: Acknowledgment that faculty cannot always verify originality of student work (limits of verification), without saying staff will not police.

units.why: "Faculty members are encouraged to explore alternative assessment approaches" is a recommendation to redesign assessment because of AI (P35). "Encouraged" gives modality should.
units.anchor: Faculty members are encouraged to explore alternative assessment approaches

units.why: The same sentence encourages "technology tools that promote academic integrity and facilitate the identification of AI-generated content". This recommends tools to identify AI content, so P40 (identification tools), not P35 which is the assessment half of the sentence.
units.anchor: technology tools that promote academic integrity and facilitate the identification of AI-generated content

units.why: "faculty members and students to be aware of the licensing agreements and terms of service" of AI models concerns terms of use and licensing (P52). Addressed to both groups so actor is all; "essential" gives should.

units.why: "Different language models may have varying usage restrictions, and compliance with ethical and legal guidelines is crucial." Requires compliance with ethical and legal guidelines, so P77. Chosen over P52 because it states a general compliance duty rather than naming licensing.
units.anchor: compliance with ethical and legal
units.policy: Compliance with ethical and legal guidelines is crucial when using AI language models, which may have varying usage restrictions.

units.why: "Faculty members are encouraged to refer to official documentation provided by the language model's developers" tells faculty to consult vendor terms. Guidance on terms of use for faculty, so P52 with modality should.

units.why: "Standards specific to the dissemination of scholarly products in various venues are likewise essential" points to venue rules for conferences and journals, so it is about scholarship (P62).
units.anchor: Standards specific to the dissemination of scholarly products in various venues are likewise essential
units.policy: Standards specific to the dissemination of scholarly products in various venues (conferences, journals) are essential.

units.why: "the policy in the syllabus should be explicitly stated with reference to the university Academic Dishonesty Policy" requires an AI statement in the syllabus, so P09. Phase is course-start because it concerns communicating expectations.

units.why: "Faculty members have the flexibility to choose from the following options" hands the choice among three syllabus statements to each instructor (P04). It is why the document is coded delegates.

units.why: The Not Permitted option says assistance from AI "is not allowed for any activities or assignments". A blanket course ban on AI, so P01 (default prohibition), must-not for students.
units.anchor: is not allowed for any activities or assignments

units.why: "the use of AI-generated content is strictly prohibited" with "original work of the student" forbids submitting AI-generated content as own work (P19). P01 covers the blanket ban in the preceding unit; this is the submission-level rule.
units.anchor: original work of the student, and the use of AI-generated content is strictly prohibited
units.policy: All submissions must be the original work of the student, and the use of AI-generated content is strictly prohibited.

units.why: "Possible disciplinary action for violations of this course policy is described in the university's Academic Dishonesty Policy" ties AI violations to the existing integrity process (P36). The sentence is repeated in all three options and is coded once here. It names no concrete penalty, so not P37.
units.anchor: disciplinary action for violations of this course policy is described in the university's Academic Dishonesty

units.why: Option 2 allows AI "only for specified activities or assignments", a narrow, instructor-specified permission. It is a named tier of use (P05) rather than a default ban, and unit_stance is restrict.

units.policy: Students cite the specific language model and platform employed, following the citation guidelines of APA, MLA, or another relevant academic style.
